read.thesis: RTX raised FY25 adjusted sales to $86.5-87B and EPS to $6.10-6.20 on record $251B backlog (book-to-bill 1.63), but kept FCF at $7-7.5B on inventory stocking and flagged supply chain as the binding constraint.

capex.quote: We've got a healthy level of CapEx invested -- expected this year, $2.5 billion to $2.7 billion

triggers.label: Capex $600M+ capacity expansion this year
triggers.quote: investing over $600 million this year in expansion projects

triggers.label: FY25 EPS raised to $6.10-6.20
triggers.quote: All in, we now see adjusted EPS at a new range of between $6.10 and $6.20 for the full year, up from our prior range of $5.80 to $5.95.

triggers.label: Stocking offsets FCF upside
triggers.quote: there's been some stocking there to prepare for this continued growth

triggers.label: Supply chain is the binding constraint
triggers.quote: It's are we going to get the supply chain in a healthy enough place to be able to deliver at these higher rates.

triggers.label: Aftermarket pricing 'appropriately aggressive'
triggers.quote: I think both have been appropriately aggressive in pricing this year.

guidance.quote: we are raising our full year adjusted sales outlook to a range of $86.5 billion to $87 billion
All in, we now see adjusted EPS at a new range of between $6.10 and $6.20 for the full year
On free cash flow, we are on track to achieve our outlook of between $7 billion and $7.5 billion for the year.
we now expect commercial aftermarket sales to grow mid-teens year-over-year, up from our prior outlook of low teens
putting Pratt in a position to deliver about 30% MRO output growth for the year
we now expect operating profit growth between $400 million and $450 million versus 2024
we now expect operating profit growth between $325 million and $375 million versus 2024
We've got a healthy level of CapEx invested -- expected this year, $2.5 billion to $2.7 billion

red_flags.label: Tariff headwind ~$90M per segment in Q3
red_flags.quote: Collins saw about $90 million of headwind from year-over-year tariffs, actually same number that Pratt saw for the quarter

red_flags.label: Inventory stocking, less reduction
red_flags.quote: we're seeing a little bit of growth in the inventory, I'd say less reduction in the inventory.

red_flags.label: GTF compensation payments $1.1-1.3B
red_flags.quote: We said between $1.1 billion and $1.3 billion for the year.

evasions.quote: So while performance has stabilized and been good, we need to continue to see that accelerate '26 and beyond because the demand is there.
